findings.summary: SPEC-0002 fails its own new rule: SDD-V060 reports the specification approval as dated after implementation began. validate --all returns 1 error and the B2 self-check IT-005/006 fails. This blocks D10 under the stated eligibility criteria.
Gate separation is sound. SDD-V059 governs specification approval, SDD-V020 governs R4/R5 implementation readiness, and UT-035 asserts the latter is unchanged and not re-reported as the former.
Every rejection path is exercised: absent, malformed, not approved, ai actor, cross-specification evidence, and unpermitted role. Each returns a distinct reason and none echoes artefact content.
Gate 1 at R4/R5 requires Product Owner AND Solution Architect and remains unenforced. Named explicitly in VALIDATION_RULES.md as not covered, so it is a known gap rather than an assumed one.
The cross-specification check reads evidenceRef text. A record with no evidenceRef cannot be caught this way; the field is free text and not a structural binding.

notes: REQUEST_CHANGES because a blocking condition now exists, not because the implementation is wrong. The implementation is correct; it correctly indicts the specification that commissioned it.
The only legitimate routes are a human-approved scoped exception under docs/sdd/VALIDATION_EXCEPTIONS.md, or a human decision to accept the failing state. Softening SDD-V060 is not one of them.
Reviewed under an actor distinct from the implementing session b3-approval-enforcement and the tester, per SDD-V051.
This is an AI review and satisfies no human gate.
